name: Berobenatide

lead: Berobenatide is Pfizer's long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight management. People follow it for appetite-driven fat loss with a monthly dosing schedule.

As a GLP-1 agonist it is expected to act like others in the class: lower appetite and slower gastric emptying, then weight loss and a leaner body. Two phase 3 trials are registered, in people with sleep apnea and overweight or obesity and in women with stress urinary incontinence and overweight or obesity; no results have been published.

paras: The registry describes monthly dosing by injection, and it is available only within clinical trials.
Human safety data have not been published. It is an unapproved investigational drug.

web.title: Pfizer's acquired monthly weight loss drug meets endpoints in Phase IIb trial - Clinical Trials Arena

angle.text: Berobenatide is Pfizer's investigational monthly GLP-1 injection, followed by fat-loss readers for its dosing frequency. Like others in its class it is meant to lower appetite and drive weight loss toward a leaner body. Phase 3 trials are registered with no results yet.

lead: Berobenatide, also written PF-08653944, PF'3944 and MET-097i, is an investigational long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that Pfizer is developing for weight management. The look-related payoff is fat loss: drugs in this class reduce appetite and body weight, and people who lose fat become leaner in the body and face. What distinguishes this candidate is a dosing interval described as monthly in trial registrations, which sponsors position as a convenience over weekly GLP-1 injections [1][2][3]. It is not approved anywhere.

The compound was developed by Metsera as MET-097i, and Pfizer acquired Metsera in November 2025 for about 10 billion dollars after a bidding war with Novo Nordisk [3]. In the Phase 2b VESPER-3 study, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled 64-week trial in adults with overweight or obesity but without type 2 diabetes, participants switched from weekly to monthly injections after 12 weeks. Mean placebo-adjusted weight loss at week 28 was 10 percent in one cohort and 12.3 percent in another, and the weight loss had not plateaued, according to a trade-press report of Pfizer's topline release [3].

Two Phase 3 trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov study berobenatide in adults with obstructive sleep apnea and overweight or obesity (VESPER-OSA 1) and in women with stress urinary incontinence and overweight or obesity [1][2]. Pfizer has said further Phase 3 trials, including weekly and monthly dosing programs in obesity, are under way or planned [3].

paras: MET-097i originated at Metsera, and Pfizer completed the acquisition in November 2025 for roughly 10 billion dollars after competing with Novo Nordisk [3]. Pfizer's VESPER program includes VESPER-1 (weekly dosing, Phase 2b), VESPER-3 (monthly maintenance) and Phase 3 trials such as VESPER-4 (weekly), VESPER-5 (weekly in type 2 diabetes) and VESPER-6 (monthly) [3].

The registered Phase 3 trials are VESPER-OSA 1 (NCT07823608), recruiting about 258 adults with sleep-disordered breathing and overweight or obesity who use positive airway pressure, with a registered start of September 2026, and NCT07932925, which plans about 900 women with stress urinary incontinence and overweight or obesity [1][2].

As a GLP-1 receptor agonist it is expected to act like other drugs in the class, which reduce appetite and slow gastric emptying. The trial registry describes the drug as given monthly in VESPER-OSA 1 [2].

Through week 28 of VESPER-3, the drug was reported as well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the GLP-1 class. Earlier interim data from September 2025 showed nausea and vomiting risk differences of 13 and 11 percent versus placebo with minimal diarrhoea [3].

No community discussion of berobenatide in looksmaxxing forums was found. It is discussed in industry coverage as a pipeline member of the GLP-1 class used for weight loss [3]. It is an unapproved investigational drug.

Phase 2b VESPER-3 reported placebo-adjusted weight loss of 10 percent and 12.3 percent at week 28 in two monthly-maintenance cohorts [3]. Phase 3 trials in sleep apnea and in stress urinary incontinence with overweight or obesity are registered [1][2]. Full peer-reviewed results were not found.

timeline.event: Pfizer acquires Metsera, the developer of MET-097i, in November. [3]
VESPER-3 topline Phase 2b results reported; VESPER-OSA 1 Phase 3 registered with a September start. [2][3]
